library(diseasy)

# Introduction

Every model in `diseasy` contains some parameterisation of its forecasts.
These parameters can then be optimised to align model forecasts with the
real-world observations.

This operation requires only two components:
1) A metric for the optimiser to optimise
2) Free parameters for the optimiser to control

# Model parameterisation
Models `diseasy` will contain parameters that are either specific to the model
(e.g. the compartment structure in `?DiseasyModelOdeSeir`) or parameters meant
to control the functional modules passed to the model (e.g. `?DiseasySeason`).

For example, lets consider the parameters of `?DiseasyModelG0`:
```{r DiseasyModelG0 - parameters}
model <- DiseasyModelG0$new()
model$parameters
```

This model has parameters inherent to the model and parameters related to the
season module. This latter type of parameters, parameters that should modify
the internal modules are treated specially:
If these parameters are `NULL` they will inherit the defaults (if any) from the
module. If they are different from `NULL` they will be applied to the module.

A couple of examples:
```{r DiseasyModelG0 - controlling season}
# We create a default season module which includes a "no seasonality" scenario
# with no parameters
season <- DiseasySeason$new(reference_date = Sys.Date())

model_1 <- DiseasyModelG0$new(season = season)
print(model_1$parameters)


# If we change to the "covid_season_v1" season model, we have a single "scale"
# parameter in the season model
season$use_covid_season_v1()

model_2 <- DiseasyModelG0$new(season = season)
print(model_2$parameters) # ... and this scale is copied to the model


# If we change to the "cosine_Season" season model, we have both a "scale"
# parameter and a "peak" parameter in the season model
season$use_cosine_season()

model_3 <- DiseasyModelG0$new(season = season)
print(model_3$parameters) # ... and these are copied to the model


# If we provide specific values to the model, then these values are
# passed to the season module.
model_4 <- DiseasyModelG0$new(
  season = season,
  parameters = list("season.scale" = 0.5)
)
print(model_4$parameters) # "peak" value is still copied
print(attr(model_4$season$model_t, "dots"))
```

# Marking parameters for optimisation

Any parameter set to `NA` is considered to be "marked for optimisation" meaning
that the fitting routine will attempt to estimate the parameter under the scoring
metric.

The default value for the parameter is stored as an attribute on any `NA` parameter
and will be used as the starting point for the optimisation.

```{r DiseasyModelG0 - parameters marked for optimisation}
model_5 <- DiseasyModelG0$new(
  season = season,
  parameters = list("season.scale" = NA) # Mark for optimisation
)
print(model_5$parameters[["season.scale"]])
```


# The scoring metric
The principal metric used in `diseasy` is the likelihood which compares the
model forecast with observations for each time-point at each strata and computes
the mean likelihood across the strata for the given time-point.

Different observation have different distributions and therefore `diseasy`
supports multiple methods for computing the likelihood given the underlying
(assumed) distribution.

The scoring of the forecasts are controlled by the `?DiseasyScoring` module,
where users can define the scoring metric and which includes a method to
compute the likelihood for a given set of model trajectories
(i.e. the output from `$get_results()`).

```{r DiseasyScoring}
scoring <- DiseasyScoring$new()

scoring
```

The scoring metric can be controlled with the `?DiseasyScoring$set_noise_model()`
method:
```{r DiseasyScoring - negative binomial}
scoring$set_noise_model("negative binomial", overdispersion = 2)

scoring
```

With the scoring metric defined, we can compute the likelihood for a set of
model trajectories with `?DiseasyScoring$compute_likelihood()`:

```{r DiseasyScoring - compute_likelihood, eval = rlang::is_installed("duckdb")}
observables <- DiseasyObservables$new(
  diseasystore = "simulist",
  conn = \() DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), ":memory:")
)

observables$set_last_queryable_date(as.Date("2020-03-01"))

model <- DiseasyModelG0$new(
  observables = observables
)

trajectories <- model$get_results(observable = "n_admission", prediction_length = 7)

model$scoring$compute_likelihood(trajectories)
```
